title: Trump: Ivanka Trump lies in sworn testimony to DC Attorney General's office
description_short: Trump: Ivanka Trump lies in sworn testimony to DC Attorney General's office
description_medium: AP reports that Ivanka Trump testified under oath for more than five hours in the D.C. attorney general’s civil suit over alleged misuse of inaugural funds. The lawsuit alleged more than $1 million in improper payments to the Trump hotel. The report confirms a deposition, but identifies no false answer or finding of perjury; the transcript or an official finding is needed to support the title’s accusation.
description_long: In December 2020, Ivanka Trump gave a deposition lasting more than five hours in a civil lawsuit brought by the District of Columbia attorney general over spending by Donald Trump’s 2017 inaugural committee. The suit alleged that the committee improperly used nonprofit donations, including by paying more than $1 million to the Trump International Hotel in Washington during inauguration week. Ivanka Trump called the inquiry wasteful and said the hotel had been told to charge a fair market rate. The Associated Press reported that she testified but did not publish her answers or identify an answer shown to be knowingly false. It reported no perjury charge or official finding that she lied under oath. The documented event is her testimony in a civil case about alleged inaugural-fund payments; it does not substantiate the title’s accusation. A deposition transcript or an official or judicial finding identifying a specific false answer would be needed to support a claim of perjury.

title: Trump Weaponized DOJ Conspiracy Theory Collapses as Hunter Biden Charged
description_short: Trump Weaponized DOJ Conspiracy Theory Collapses as Hunter Biden Charged
description_medium: Throughout 2023, Trump and Republicans relentlessly promoted the false claim that the DOJ was weaponized against Republicans while protecting Hunter Biden. The claim was undercut when Hunter Biden was charged with federal gun crimes and tax evasion. Despite months of House Republican investigations, no evidence emerged of Biden directing DOJ decisions. The disinformation campaign was designed to delegitimize Trump prosecutions by false equivalence and manufactured outrage.
description_long: The linked Washington Post report is dated October 2022, before the 2023 disputes described by this entry. It reports that federal agents investigating Hunter Biden believed they had evidence supporting tax charges and a false statement related to a gun purchase. The article says Delaware U.S. Attorney David Weiss, a Trump administration holdover, would decide whether to file charges. It does not examine whether President Joe Biden directed Justice Department decisions, describe the findings of House Republicans’ 2023 investigations, or test claims of political weaponization. Hunter Biden’s later federal charges show that the investigation proceeded to prosecution, but that outcome alone does not resolve broader questions about the department’s independence or establish that political officials directed case decisions. The linked source supports only the narrower account of investigators’ assessment and the prosecutor’s role at that time. Records of DOJ communications, charging decisions, congressional findings and the later proceedings would be needed to evaluate the claims in the title and populated medium.

notes: The linked Washington Post report was read. Published in October 2022, it says federal agents believed they had evidence to charge Hunter Biden with tax crimes and a false statement related to a gun purchase, with U.S. Attorney David Weiss to decide whether to bring charges. It predates the 2023 claims about DOJ direction and does not assess whether Joe Biden directed prosecutorial decisions or what House investigations found. Those claims require contemporaneous 2023 records and findings; the linked article cannot substantiate them.
